collections.label: Handyman
collections.desc: {n} free handyman website templates with HTML code: booking panels with arrival windows, service-area maps, job lists, sample rates and quote forms.
collections.intro: A handyman site has one job: turn a visitor with a dripping tap or a sagging gutter into a booked visit. These {n} templates come from our plumbing, electrical, roofing, HVAC, building, landscaping, cleaning and pest-control sets, picked for the layouts that put the phone number, the jobs you take and a visit request first. Mix the trades you cover into one service list and keep the booking panel above the fold.
lookFor: A visible phone number and a call button that stay on screen on a phone.
A visit-request form with job types and arrival windows, so people book instead of calling around.
A service-area map or list of areas, which answers "do you come to me?" before anyone asks.
Sample rates or a call-out fee, and a short list of recent jobs as proof of work.
Licence and insurance lines filled in with your own details.
faq: What should a handyman website include?

A clear list of the jobs you take, the areas you cover, how to book (form, call or text), when you can come, sample prices or a call-out fee, and a few recent jobs. The dispatch layouts in this collection put all of that on one page.
Can one template cover several trades?
Yes. Pick the layout you like and replace its service cards and job chips with the trades you offer; the plumbing, electrical and building designs share the same structure.
Does the booking form work out of the box?
No. Forms are static sample markup. Connect your own form service, booking tool or email handler before you publish.

collections.label: Personal site
collections.desc: {n} free personal website templates with HTML code: name-as-masthead portfolios, project indexes, case studies, CV sections and contact blocks.
collections.intro: A personal website is a short answer to "who are you and what have you made?". These {n} templates come from our personal portfolio, developer, designer, photographer and coaching sets, picked for layouts that lead with your name and your work rather than a sales pitch: a large masthead, a project index you can scan in seconds, one case study told in steps, and a plain way to get in touch.
lookFor: Your name and one line about what you do, readable in the first screen.
A project list that is easy to scan, with a filter if you work across disciplines.
One case study told in steps, which says more than a dozen thumbnails.
A short CV or services block and a contact line people can copy.
A layout that still reads well when you only have three projects.
faq: What should go on a personal website?
Your name and what you do, three to six pieces of work, one deeper case study, a short CV or list of services, and a way to contact you. The index and work layouts here are built around exactly that.
Do I need a portfolio to use these?
No. Swap the project cards for writing, talks or a list of services; the type-led layouts work with text alone.
Can I host it for free?
Yes. Each template is a single HTML page, so it runs on any static host. You can also pass the HTML and DESIGN.md to an AI coding agent to extend it.

collections.label: One page
collections.desc: {n} free one-page website templates with HTML code, picked across every industry: full-width bands, split heroes, tile mosaics and magazine layouts.
collections.intro: Every template on Made Good Designs is a complete one-page site, so this collection is a tour of the layouts rather than the industries: {n} picks spread across every industry, covering full-width colour bands, split heroes with a next-step card, rounded tile mosaics and magazine-style pages. Pick the structure first, then the sub-niche that is closest to your business for the right sections and copy.
lookFor: A clear order of sections: what you do, proof, how it works, prices or options, questions, contact.
Sticky navigation that jumps to each section, since there are no other pages.
One main call to action repeated at the top and the bottom.
A layout that keeps working on a phone, where a long page is the norm.
Room to grow: section blocks you can copy into a second page later.
faq: Is a one-page website enough for a small business?
For most local and service businesses, yes: one page can carry your services, proof, prices, questions and contact. Add pages later for a menu, listings or a blog if you need them.
Is a one-page site bad for SEO?
Not if each section has real headings and text. It targets fewer keywords than a multi-page site, so give your main service and location a clear heading.
What is the difference between these layouts?

Band layouts use full-width colour sections and big numbered steps; atlas layouts use a split hero and card grids; bento layouts use a tile mosaic; folio layouts read like a magazine with ruled lists and no cards.

collections.label: Simple
collections.desc: {n} free simple website templates with HTML code: minimal and monochrome designs with quiet layouts, plenty of white space and one clear next step.
collections.intro: Simple is harder than it looks: fewer elements means each one has to be right. These {n} templates are our minimal and monochrome designs, picked for the quietest layouts in each industry: a task-first hero with three clear doors, one column of services, generous spacing and a restrained palette. They are the easiest starting point if you want a site that feels calm and loads fast.
lookFor: One clear thing to do on the first screen, not five.
A single typeface or a tight pair, and a small colour palette.
Enough white space that each section stands on its own.
Short sections you can delete without breaking the layout.
Plain HTML and CSS, so the page stays light.
faq: What makes a website template simple?
A small number of sections, one clear call to action, a restrained palette and one or two fonts. The minimal and monochrome designs here keep to that.
Are simple templates good for beginners?
Yes. With fewer components there is less to edit, and the DESIGN.md lists every colour and font in one place so changes stay consistent.
Can I add more sections later?
Yes. The section blocks share the same tokens, so new sections inherit the same colours, type and spacing.

collections.label: Professional
collections.desc: {n} free professional website templates with HTML code for firms, clinics and agencies: information-first layouts, service lists, fee tables and contact forms.
collections.intro: A professional site has to earn trust before it asks for anything. These {n} templates come from our legal, accounting, advisory, insurance, healthcare, property and B2B software sets, in corporate, minimal and editorial styles, picked for information-first layouts: hours and contact in a fixed sidebar, services and fees in tables, a timeline of how you work, and a calm consultation form.
lookFor: Who you are and who you help, stated plainly in the first screen.
Services and fees set out in a table or list people can compare.
Credentials, registration numbers and memberships (filled in with your own).
A clear next step: book a consultation, request a call or send documents.
A restrained style that reads as serious on a phone as on a desktop.
faq: What makes a website look professional?
Consistent type and spacing, a restrained palette, plain language, clear contact details and real credentials. The corporate and editorial designs here are built on those rules.
Are these suitable for law firms and clinics?
Yes, as designs. They include fee tables, practice areas and consultation forms, but they are not legal or medical advice and do not make a site compliant with any professional rule.
Can I change the colours to my brand?
Yes. Every colour is a token in the DESIGN.md, so changing the primary and accent updates buttons, links and highlights across the page.

collections.label: Modern
collections.desc: {n} free modern website templates with HTML code: tile mosaics, full-width colour bands, oversized headlines and type-led layouts, newest first.
collections.intro: These {n} templates are the most current-looking designs we have made, newest first: tile mosaics with floating pill navigation, full-width colour bands with oversized headlines, type-led project indexes, one-home showcases and dark class timetables, plus our SaaS and AI pages in their sharpest styles. They suit businesses that want to look current without a trend that dates in a year.
lookFor: A strong first screen: one big headline and one clear action.
Rounded tiles or full-width bands that break the page into easy chunks.
Large, confident type with a tight palette.
Motion kept subtle, so the page stays fast and accessible.
A dark theme, which many visitors now expect.
faq: What makes a website template look modern?
Large headlines, generous spacing, bento-style tiles or full-width bands, a small palette and a dark mode. The designs here use those patterns.
Will a modern design date quickly?
Layout trends change, but the tokens in the DESIGN.md make a refresh cheap: change the fonts, radius and colours in one place.
Do these templates have a dark mode?
Yes. Every template ships light and dark colour tokens.

collections.label: Booking
collections.desc: {n} free booking website templates with HTML code: table booking panels with time slots, class timetables, visit requests with arrival windows and task-first layouts.
collections.intro: When a site exists to take bookings, the booking panel should be the hero, not a link in the footer. These {n} templates are our booking-first layouts: a table booking panel with time slots for restaurants and cafes, a weekly class timetable for gyms and studios, a visit request with arrival windows for trades, and task-first pages for clinics, salons, stays and garages.
lookFor: The booking panel or timetable in the first screen.
Times, prices and policies shown before someone commits.
A short form: name, contact, time, and only what you really need.
A clear cancellation or deposit policy in plain words.
A phone fallback for people who would rather call.
faq: Do these templates include a working booking system?
No. The booking panels, timetables and visit forms are static designs. Connect the booking tool or calendar you already use, or ask an AI coding agent to wire one up from the HTML.
Which layout fits my business?

Restaurants and cafes: the table booking layout. Gyms, yoga and dance studios: the class timetable. Trades: the visit request with arrival windows. Clinics, salons, hotels and garages: the task-first layouts.
Can I show prices next to time slots?
Yes. The sample prices are placeholders set to zero; replace them with your own.

collections.label: Small business
collections.desc: {n} free small business website templates with HTML code for local shops, salons, trades, garages and offices: hours, phone, services, prices and directions.
collections.intro: Most visitors to a small business site want three things: are you open, what do you do, and how do I reach you. These {n} templates come from our local-business sets, one per sub-niche (bakeries, cafes, florists, barbers, salons, garages, car washes, cleaners, landscapers, accountants and more), picked for layouts that put opening hours, the phone number and the services first.
lookFor: Opening hours, address and phone number in the first screen or a fixed sidebar.
A short, scannable list of services with sample prices.
Reviews or proof, kept honest and attributed (add your own).
A map or directions section, and parking or access notes.
Fast load on a phone, since most local searches happen there.
faq: What should a small business website include?
Hours, address, phone, a list of services with prices, a few photos or proof of work, answers to common questions and a contact form. The atlas and ledger layouts here put those first.
Is a template enough for a small business?
For most local businesses, yes. Start from the closest sub-niche, replace the sample copy, and add pages only when you need them.
Do I need a developer?
Not for small edits: the HTML is plain and the DESIGN.md lists every colour and font. For bigger changes, an AI coding agent can work from the same files.

collections.label: Home bakery
collections.desc: {n} free home bakery website templates with HTML code: priced menus with dietary keys, pre-order panels, specials boards and pickup details.
collections.intro: A home bakery sells by pre-order and pickup, so the site needs a menu with prices, a way to order ahead and clear pickup or delivery details more than it needs a dining room. These {n} templates start with our bakery designs and add the cafe, catering and food-truck layouts that suit small food businesses, in warm retro, playful and editorial styles.
lookFor: A priced menu with a dietary and allergen key (check every item yourself).
An order-ahead or pre-order panel with pickup days and times.
Pickup address, delivery area and payment options stated plainly.
Photos or drawings of your bakes, replaced with your own.
Any licence or registration lines your area requires, filled in by you.
faq: What should a home bakery website include?
A menu with prices, how and when to order, pickup or delivery details, allergen notes, a few photos of your bakes and a contact line. The menu and booking layouts here are a good base.
Can I take orders through these templates?
The order and booking panels are static designs. Connect a form, ordering or payment service you trust before you take real orders.
Do I need a licence to sell baked goods from home?
Rules differ by country and region. The templates leave licence and registration lines for you to fill in; check your local rules.

collections.label: Dark mode
collections.desc: {n} free dark website templates with HTML code, shown in their dark theme. Each one ships light and dark colour tokens in its DESIGN.md.
collections.intro: Every template here has a dark theme built in, not inverted after the fact: its DESIGN.md carries a full set of dark colour tokens for every role. These {n} picks, spread across industries, are the designs whose accent colours glow most on a dark background, shown in their dark theme. Use them as a dark site, or keep both themes and follow the visitor's system setting.
lookFor: Body text that stays readable: off-white on near-black, not pure white on pure black.
An accent colour that keeps its contrast on dark surfaces.
Images and illustrations that do not glare against the background.
A theme switch, or a page that follows the visitor's system setting.
Borders and surfaces in slightly lighter greys, so cards still separate.
faq: Do these templates come in light mode too?
Yes. Each DESIGN.md has light and dark tokens; the dark theme is what these pictures show.
How do I make the site follow the visitor's dark mode setting?
Use the dark tokens inside a prefers-color-scheme: dark media query, or add a theme switch. The tokens are named the same in both themes, so only the values change.
Are dark websites harder to read?
They can be if contrast is too high or too low. Check the text and button colours with a contrast checker after you change any token.
